h: The Joy of Torah at the Shabbos Table

p: At all the meals of Shabbos
at night, "Great joy will come," etc.;
in the morning, "in which the soul will rejoice,"
The matter is according to what they said
that at the end of Yom Kippur
a Heavenly voice came forth and said to them:
your prayer has already been heard";
and it is brought in the Rishonim.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּסַיֵּים הַפָּסוּק (קֹהֶלֶת ט, ז)
And it is as the pasuk concludes (Koheles 9:7):
כִּי כְבָר רָצָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ
"for God has already accepted your deeds."
and drink your wine with a merry heart."
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good"
regarding everything that is the opposite of good;
that is, then, at the entrance of Shabbos,
at the end of the sixth day,
Hashem Yisbarach saw that everything is
such that it will be very good.
And of Shabbos it is written (Bereishis 2:2):
and Targum Yerushalmi renders "and He desired";
that then, at the entrance of Shabbos,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם, ט, ד)
And as they said (Bereishis Rabbah there, 9:4):
if only you would find favor before Me
as you have found favor before Me
גַּם כֵּן בְּשִׂמְחָה זוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
is also with this joy, as mentioned above:
כִּי כְבָר רָצָה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ
"for God has already accepted your deeds."
"a person establishes his meal over wine"
"And wine that gladdens the heart of man."
And in the holy Zohar there is seemingly
and drink of the wine I have mixed'
this is the bread of the Written Torah,
and the wine of the Oral Torah";
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רמ, א)
it is stated: "The Torah is wine and milk,
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah";
and there the marginal note explains:
and milk is the Written Torah.
אַךְ לְפִי שִׁטְחִיּוּת לְשׁוֹן הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
But according to the plain wording of the holy Zohar,
that wine refers to the Written Torah
and milk to the Oral Torah.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג ד, א)
And so it is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 4a):
יֵינִי עִם חֲלָבִי (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, א)
And Yaakov is the "body," as is known,
and he is the attribute of Truth,
the aspect of the Written Torah;
and Shlomo is the aspect of lower Chochmah,
and "my milk" as the Oral Torah.
And as for its calling the Oral Torah
it is that the Oral Torah
"And as for Me, this is My covenant with them," etc.,
"and My words which I have put in your mouth";
וְזֶה קָאֵי עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this refers to the Oral Torah,
which is called "the word of Hashem"
"for by the mouth of these words
I have made a covenant with you"
for the sake of the words that are oral."
And likewise in the Gemara (Avodah Zarah 35a)
"The words of Your beloved ones are sweeter to me
than the wine of the Torah";
and that is the Written Torah.
But in truth, what they expounded
in the Ra'aya Mehemna cited above,
יַיִן מָסָכְתִּי עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
"the wine I have mixed" as the Oral Torah,
is from the precision of the wording,
that it said "the wine I have mixed"
as it said "eat of my bread";
that the intent is the Oral Torah,
which is called "the wine I have mixed":
into the hearts of the Sages,
for in truth it is the words of the living God,
"and My words which I have put in your mouth";
only to the Sages it appears
that they innovate from their own hearts.
Therefore it says "the wine I have mixed."
And it is as it says (Devarim 32:2):
"My speech shall distill as the dew":
which is not noticed at the time it descends
and so is the Oral Torah.
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא יַיִן
the Written Torah is also called wine,
and it is what is called "my wine,"
just as it is called "my bread";
only, there is Torah that is like bread,
"and bread that sustains the heart of man";
וְיֵשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא בִּבְחִינַת יַיִן הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ
and there is Torah that is in the aspect of wine that gladdens,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ מַהֲרַ״ל מִפְּרָאג זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as the Maharal of Prague, of blessed memory, explained
"A lot whets the appetite, a little sustains"
and it is the aspect of Yaakov,
who himself is called the wine,
for he is the aspect of Truth,
וְלָכֵן נִדְרָשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
Therefore it is expounded in the holy Zohar cited above:
"I have drunk my wine" as the Written Torah,
And therefore at the two meals
which alludes to the Oral Torah;
so that through the wine of Kiddush
which is "the wine I have mixed," as mentioned above.
And this is "Go, eat your bread with joy,
and drink your wine with a merry heart":
הַיְינוּ הַיַּיִן שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הָאָדָם
that is, the wine called by man's name,
and it is "the wine I have mixed,"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִים לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
through which one merits the Oral Torah.
Which is not so at the third meal,
they did not institute Kiddush over wine.
to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin."
are those who keep the three meals on Shabbos,
who are called "members of the King's palace,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב רנב, ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 252b);
"to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin."
וְלָכֵן לֹא תִּקְּנוּ בִּסְעוּדָה זוֹ יַיִן
Therefore they did not institute wine at this meal;
and likewise the joy is of itself:
in which is the Will of Wills."
